admitting officer                                                                                           Comment [MG1]: The Admitting Officer

Emergency Department
Newtown Hospital


[Date of the letter]


Dear Admitting Officer,
Re: Ms Sally McConville, aged 38


I am writing to refer MsMcConville, who has a 2-day history of severe shortness of breath, for urgent       Comment [MG2]: severe respiratory
management and investigations.                                                                              distress with possible pneumonia




On today's review, MsMcConville presented with shortness of breath at rest, fever and an increased work
of breathing. Despite taking cortisone and antibiotics, her symptoms have worsened. The examination
showed widespread wheeze and bi-basal crepitations, which indicates acute asthma with possible              Comment [MG3]: wheezes
pneumonia. Please note, we tried to control her condition with Ventolin Nebules with no improvement.        Comment [MG4]: indicate



MsMcConville's condition started three days ago with slight fever, a productive cough and a wheezy chest.
[There was no shortness of breath]. One day later, MsMcConville developed severe shortness and
exacerbation of her wheeze. The fever also exacerbated and reached 38 C˚.                                   Comment [MG5]: wheezes



MsMcConville has asthma, depression and hypertension for which she takes ramipril, 2.5mg; paroxetine,
20mg; fluticasone inhaler, 250; and Ventolin inhaler. She is a non-smoker with no known allergies.



In light of the above, I would be grateful if you could immediately admit Ms McConville to The Emergency
Department and provide her with the required treatment as soon as possible. Should there be any
queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.



Yours faithfully,

Doctor

MsMcConville has asthma, depression and hypertension for which she takes ramipril, 2.5mg; paroxetine,
20mg; fluticasone inhaler, 250; and Ventolin inhaler. She is a non-smoker with no known allergies.

In light of the above, I would be grateful if you could immediately admit Ms McConville to The Emergency
Department and provide her with the required treatment as soon as possible. Should there be any
queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours faithfully,

Doctor
